subject: Post-call: encryption model access & operational asks (PII, retention, KMS options)
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acmehealth.com>, security@acmehealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Dec 2027 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: encryption model access & operational asks (PII, retention, KMS options)

Hi Samantha / Acme security team —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and the follow-up items we promised on encryption and data controls. I tried to separate product answers vs. operational next steps so you can route to your procurement/security owners quickly.

Summary (short):
- In-transit: All API traffic to Redwood defaults to TLS 1.3. We can support mTLS for dedicated/private deployments.
- At-rest: Model weights and customer payloads are encrypted at rest; for hosted customers we use service-managed envelope keys.
- Customer-managed keys (BYOK): Supported for Dedicated and Private. Options: KMS integration (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) or HSM-backed key import for on-prem HSM.
- PII handling: We offer configurable request-level redaction and configurable retention windows. For Acme we recommend short retention (30d) + explicit retention policy on logs.
- Logging/audit: Token-level telemetry available in the Console; we can suppress PII from logs and provide export of audit records to your S3/GCS bucket.

Action items we agreed on:
1) Acme security to send the top 8 compliance questions you need answered (encryption, key custody, audit retention, incident response, data flow diagrams).
2) Redwood to provide SOC2 summary + example KMS integration diagram and a proposed retention matrix (we'll attach).
3) Evaluate BYOK for Dedicated vs. Private with Acme infra team — we proposed a short workshop next week to model traffic and latency impact.

Quick asks for you to unblock us:
- Which deployment mode are you evaluating first (Hosted API with BYOK? Dedicated? Private VPC)?
- Do you have a preferred cloud KMS provider or on-prem HSM vendor?

I'll attach the SOC2 summary and a draft KMS integration diagram for now. Ben/Laura — adding you for pricing and procurement timing.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0197

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, kms-integration-draft.png

From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acmehealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Health Security <security@acmehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Dec 2027 17:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: encryption model access & operational asks (PII, retention, KMS options)

Thanks Olga — helpful summary. Quick clarifications from Security + a couple of asks before we set up the workshop: 

1) Key custody: We need to confirm that when you say "BYOK for Dedicated/Private" the private key material never leaves our HSM. Is there an option for Redwood to call a customer HSM for unwrap operations?

2) Audit trail retention: Our policy requires 7 years of access/audit logs for PHI use cases. Is that something Redwood can support via long-term export to our bucket? Any costs we should expect?

3) Live model access controls: For generated outputs, we need token-level redaction flagged as PII and a toggle to block storage of certain request/response pairs. Is that configurable per-route?

4) Encryption in-use (memory): Does Redwood offer encrypted memory/KMS-integrated attestation for KV cache or do you rely on process isolation?

We attached a short spreadsheet (acme-security-qa.xlsx) with our priority questions; happy to annotate if anything's unclear.

Samantha Ortiz
Head of Product Security, Acme Health
samantha.ortiz@acmehealth.com

Attachment: acme-security-qa.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: encryption model access & operational asks (PII, retention, KMS options)

Olga — forwarding my quick notes for the pricing/procurement thread.

Notes:
- If Acme needs 7yr audit retention exported to their bucket, that will be an add-on (log archival) in our pricing sheet. Rough estimate: $X/month at their expected throughput — will confirm after we get telemetry.
- BYOK options: (1) Cloud KMS integration (wrap/unwrap done by Redwood using customer-managed KEK) — fastest for Dedicated; (2) On-prem HSM with remote unwrap via attestation path — requires Private deployment and security workshop; (3) HSM import (Redwood holds wrapped key) — middle ground but Acme may not accept.
- Memory/encryption-in-use: our runtime currently relies on process isolation and kernel protections; we can offer platform attestations and roadmap items for encrypted memory. We'll put this in the security addendum.

I'll draft a short pricing + options matrix once we confirm deployment path. Recommend scheduling a 60-min security workshop with Acme Sec + Infra + Redwood Sec engineering next Wed or Thu (Dec 8/9) morning PT.

Ben Carter
Director, Solutions (Enterprise) | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (617) 555-0113

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acmehealth.com>, security@acmehealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 5 Dec 2027 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: encryption model access & operational asks (PII, retention, KMS options)

Samantha / Acme Sec —

Thanks for the questions and the spreadsheet. I've gone through Acme's QA and annotated high-priority items inline (attached). Short answers to the numbered items you raised: 

1) Key custody — we do support a remote unwrap flow for Private where calls to your HSM are used for runtime unwraps (no private key export). For Dedicated we support cloud KMS integrations where Redwood never stores the plaintext DEK; unwrap operations happen in a secure enclave (HSM-backed) in our environment. We'll detail the flows in the workshop.

2) Audit retention — yes, we can export audit logs to your S3 with lifecycle policies that meet 7yr retention; log archival is a separate billing line (I flagged to Ben).

3) Per-route PII toggles — available. You can mark API routes to opt-out of storage and to apply dynamic redaction rules. We will share a suggested redaction ruleset for PHI.

4) Encrypted memory — current state: process isolation + kernel protections; roadmap: attestable encrypted memory for KV cache (ETA Q2/2028). We'll include a sign-off option in the security addendum so you can select "attestation required" for Private deployment.

Next steps (concrete):
- I will upload an annotated QA (acme-security-qa-annotated.xlsx) and the SOC2 snapshot to the Drive link here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcD-kms-integration
- We propose Security Workshop: Tue, 7 Dec 2027 at 09:00 PT (60m) — please confirm attendees and a calendar invite.
- Ben will follow up with a pricing/archival estimate and a short BYOK options matrix.

If you prefer, we can run the workshop as a recording + Q&A for those who cannot join live.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai

Attachments: acme-security-qa-annotated.xlsx, redwood-soc2-summary.pdf
